concept.title: Help for the field, button or pane in use
concept.shortdesc: Besides the page, your app can tell which field has focus, which button the reader pressed last and which tab or pane they are in, so help opens on exactly the thing they are working on.

section.title: Signals, most specific first
section.p: Every help request can carry up to four signals. Each one is a context key, like the keys authors tag topics with (see ), except that the view may also be a path.

strow.stentry: The field or control that is selected or has focus now.
The button or command the reader pressed last.
The tab, pane or dialog the reader last worked in.
The page or view, as before.

section.p: The first signal that has help this reader can see wins. A signal whose key has no help falls back to its own parents before the next signal is tried, but a parent it shares with a later signal waits for that signal's turn. So with focus on settings.sso.nickname (no topic) and the settings.sso.advanced pane, the pane's topic opens rather than the general settings.sso one. See for the full order.
Authors write help for a field or button exactly as for a screen: a topic, or a section in one, tagged with a resourceid for its key. Nothing new is needed in help-contexts.yaml.

section.title: Mark up your app
section.p: With the widget (see ), add two attributes to your markup. The widget watches focus and clicks and keeps the signals up to date.

dlentry.dd: On a field, control, or a group of them. When focus is inside it, it is the focus. When the reader presses a button, link, tab, menu item, checkbox or radio button inside it, it is also the action.
On a tab panel, pane or dialog, or on the tab that shows it. Focus or a press inside it makes it the pane.

ul.li: The nearest attribute wins, and the widget looks through shadow DOM, so attributes work inside your own web components.
Focus moving to an element without a key clears focus. The last action and pane are kept until the view changes with setContext.
The help button and the panel never count, so pressing ? keeps the field the reader was on.
To open help from the keyboard while a field has focus, call OpenDHelp.open() from your own shortcut, such as F1.

section.title: While the panel is open
section.p: The open panel follows the reader: when the focus, last action or pane changes, it moves to the new help after a quarter of a second. It stops following as soon as the reader navigates inside the panel, by link or search, so it never takes away what they are reading; it follows again the next time it opens. Set follow to false in OpenDHelp.init to use activity only when the panel opens.

Opening the panel on an explicit context, with OpenDHelp.open({ key }) or <opend-help-button key="…">, opens exactly that context and ignores activity until it closes. Call open() with no argument to let activity count.

section.title: Apps that track activity themselves
section.p: If your app already knows what is selected, such as a row in a grid, a node on a canvas or a command from a menu, report it instead of, or as well as, using the attributes:
Only the signals you name change. Pass activity: false to OpenDHelp.init to stop the widget watching the page at all, so that only what you report is sent.

section.title: Rendering help in your own UI
section.p: Apps that call the JSON API (see ), and apps that are not web pages at all, send the same signals as query parameters. Any you leave out are simply not used.

The answer says which signal it used in signal (focus, action, pane or view, or null when the app default answered). A web app can let the widget do the tracking and read the signals from it, without ever opening the panel:

OpenDHelp.activity() returns only the signals that are set, for example { focus: 'settings.sso.issuer', pane: 'settings.sso.advanced', path: '/settings/sso' }. Context links on public sites take the same parameters (see ).

ul.li: Only the keys you put in data-help-key and data-help-pane, or pass to setActivity. Never what the reader typed, element text, ids or selectors, and nothing at all from elements without those attributes.
Keys longer than 256 characters are ignored, by the widget and by the server.
Signals are resolved under the same rules as every context: a key whose help the reader cannot see falls back, so a signal never reveals a hidden topic.

section.title: Check it before publishing
section.p: The previewer's help lab has fields for a focused field, last pressed button, pane and path. It shows what they resolve to for the preview reader, and which signal answered.
